title: ACA s. 9 — Interim measures by Court (ACA s. 9)

content.overview: Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 empowers a Court to grant specified interim measures before or during arbitral proceedings, and after an award but before enforcement under section 36. It also regulates commencement of arbitration after pre-arbitration interim relief and limits court intervention after constitution of the arbitral tribunal where the section 17 remedy is efficacious.
content.glance: Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 empowers a Court to grant specified interim measures before or during arbitral proceedings, and after an award but before enforcement under section 36. It also regulates commencement of arbitration after pre-arbitration interim relief and limits court intervention after constitution of the arbitral tribunal where the section 17 remedy is efficacious.
content.study:
Section 9 — Interim measures, etc., by Court

Section 9(1) permits a party, at the statutory stages specified in the provision, to apply to a Court for:
• appointment of a guardian for a minor or person of unsound mind for arbitral proceedings; or
• an interim measure of protection.

The listed interim measures include:
(a) preservation, interim custody or sale of goods that are the subject-matter of the arbitration agreement;
(b) securing the amount in dispute;
(c) detention, preservation or inspection of property or a thing that is the subject of the dispute, or concerning which a question may arise, including authority for entry, sampling, observation or experiment where necessary or expedient to obtain full information or evidence;
(d) interim injunction or appointment of a receiver; and
(e) another interim measure of protection that appears to the Court to be just and convenient.

The Court has the same power for making orders as it has for the purpose of, and in relation to, proceedings before it.

Section 9(2) addresses pre-arbitration interim relief. Where a Court passes an order under section 9(1) before arbitral proceedings commence, the arbitral proceedings must be commenced within ninety days from the date of the order, or within such further time as the Court may determine.

Section 9(3) addresses the post-constitution position. Once the arbitral tribunal has been constituted, the Court shall not entertain a section 9(1) application unless it finds circumstances exist that may not render the remedy under section 17 efficacious.

The section therefore requires close attention to timing: before arbitration, during arbitration, after award but before enforcement, and after constitution of the tribunal. The statutory availability of relief is distinct from the discretionary merits of the requested interim measure.

sections.heading: 1. Statutory stages for a section 9 application
sections.body: Section 9(1) permits an application before or during arbitral proceedings and after the arbitral award but before enforcement under section 36. The procedural stage must be identified at the outset.

sections.heading: 2. Categories of interim relief
sections.body: The section expressly covers guardianship for arbitral proceedings and specified protective measures concerning goods, security for the amount in dispute, preservation/inspection of property or things, injunctions, receivership and other measures that appear just and convenient to the Court.

sections.heading: 3. Preservation and evidentiary measures
sections.body: Section 9(1)(ii)(c) permits detention, preservation or inspection and related access, sampling, observation or experiment where necessary or expedient for obtaining full information or evidence. The relief must remain connected to the statutory subject matter.

sections.heading: 4. Pre-arbitration order and ninety-day commencement rule
sections.body: Where interim protection is granted before arbitral proceedings commence, section 9(2) requires commencement within ninety days from the order, unless the Court determines a further period.

sections.heading: 5. Section 9 after constitution of the tribunal
sections.body: Once the arbitral tribunal is constituted, section 9(3) bars entertainment of a section 9(1) application unless the Court finds circumstances that may not render the section 17 remedy efficacious.

sections.heading: 6. Court's statutory power and relief
sections.body: The Court has the same power for making orders as it has for proceedings before it. Section 9 should nevertheless be analysed as an interim protective jurisdiction rather than as a substitute adjudication of the underlying dispute.

examples.title: Pre-arbitration protection
examples.body: Before commencing arbitration, a party seeks preservation of goods that are the subject of the arbitration agreement. Section 9(1) expressly includes preservation and interim custody or sale of such goods within the potential interim measures.

examples.title: Security for amount in dispute
examples.body: A party seeks an interim measure directed to securing the amount in dispute in the arbitration. That category is expressly identified in section 9(1)(ii)(b).

examples.title: Evidence-preservation order
examples.body: A party seeks inspection and preservation of property connected with the dispute and requests necessary access and sampling to obtain full information or evidence. Section 9(1)(ii)(c) addresses such relief.

examples.title: Tribunal already constituted
examples.body: After constitution of the arbitral tribunal, a party approaches the Court under section 9. The Court must apply section 9(3) and consider whether circumstances exist showing that the section 17 remedy may not be efficacious.

examples.title: Post-award, pre-enforcement
examples.body: An arbitral award has been made but has not yet been enforced under section 36. Section 9(1) expressly includes this stage within its temporal scope.

hypotheticals.question: A Court grants section 9 relief before arbitration begins. How long does the applicant have to commence arbitral proceedings?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 9(2) requires commencement within ninety days from the date of the Court's order, unless the Court determines a further time.

hypotheticals.question: The arbitral tribunal has already been constituted and the applicant seeks the same protection under section 9. Is the application automatically entertainable?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 9(3) states that the Court shall not entertain the application unless it finds circumstances that may not render the remedy under section 17 efficacious.

hypotheticals.question: Can section 9 be invoked after an award?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, but section 9(1) places the post-award application within the period after the award and before enforcement in accordance with section 36.

hypotheticals.question: Does section 9 list only injunctions and receivers?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The statutory list also covers guardianship, preservation/custody/sale of goods, securing the amount in dispute, detention/preservation/inspection and related evidentiary measures, and other protective measures that appear just and convenient.

misconceptions.trap: Section 9 is available only before arbitration begins.
misconceptions.correction: Section 9(1) covers applications before or during arbitral proceedings and after an award but before enforcement under section 36.

misconceptions.trap: Once the tribunal is constituted, section 9 is always unavailable.
misconceptions.correction: Section 9(3) permits entertainment where the Court finds circumstances that may not render the section 17 remedy efficacious.

misconceptions.trap: A pre-arbitration section 9 order has no consequence for commencement.
misconceptions.correction: Section 9(2) requires arbitral proceedings to commence within ninety days, or within further time determined by the Court.

misconceptions.trap: Section 9 is a substitute for deciding the dispute on the merits.
misconceptions.correction: It is an interim protective jurisdiction; final adjudication remains governed by the arbitral process and applicable law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What are the principal statutory questions under section 9?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify the procedural stage; identify the statutory category of interim relief sought; establish the factual basis for protection; if the tribunal is already constituted, address section 9(3) and the efficacy of section 17; and, if relief is granted before arbitration, comply with section 9(2)'s commencement requirement.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: The statutory stage and nature of the requested protection should be identified before discretionary considerations are argued.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should counsel structure a section 9 application?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Set out the arbitration agreement and procedural stage; identify the exact section 9(1) category relied upon; demonstrate why the protective order is connected to the arbitral dispute; address section 9(2) if relief is pre-arbitration and section 9(3) if the tribunal has already been constituted; then formulate the narrow interim order sought.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: The prayer should track the statutory category and the factual necessity for protection.
